# Parcels to ask the Prep-Center about, one SHA-256 per line.
#
# Never the tracking number itself: this file is in version control, and a
# tracking number identifies a real customer's goods. The probe hashes every ID
# in the Prep-Center's manifest and matches, so it can answer "is this one
# resolvable, and what does it carry?" without the repo ever holding the answer
# to "which parcel is it?".
#
#   printf '%s' "1Z..." | sha256sum
#
# Both the upper- and lower-case spelling of the same ID are matched, so either
# hash works.

db8eac1041f5c3871ec17febdad74668dac7166f7016a4690c7be0716f80f1f8
# WH-IT-OUT-000084, box 2 — 18 chars, expected:true on their manifest, no DDT
27f129b5f2ac0c11604e6b72a790edbfbeff4cac02f1b6021e775724cc0a6b02
# WH-IT-OUT-000084, box 1 — 12 chars, a truncated label
b4739b43ce6932b8209ede28d9766e3fba9ddf9b017c96802113d174caf8be13
# WH-IT-OUT-000086, the control: same shape, same manifest, and it DID get a note
0cbc733c3e9205e8a1bfbb9a7fbacab532526f1413e105b48767f5ee54750ef2
